name: Römerweg Kitzbühel – St. Johann
kurzbeschreibung: The historic Römerweg trail follows the path of the ancient Roman road from Kitzbühel to Oberndorf, blending culture with stunning valley views.
preis: Kostenlos frei begehbar (Bahnfahrt für Teilstrecken ca. 3–4 €)
beschreibung:
Overview

The Römerweg (Roman Trail) spanning between Kitzbühel, Oberndorf in Tirol, and St. Johann in Tirol is celebrated as one of the sunniest, most historic, and scenically rewarding hillside walking routes in the Kitzbühel Alps. Tracing an ancient merchant and military transit corridor utilized since Roman antiquity to connect the Inn Valley with the Pinzgau region of Salzburg, this panoramic route undulates gently between 750 and 800 meters elevation along the sun-bathed western foot of the iconic Kitzbüheler Horn. As walkers stroll past centuries-old Tyrolean timber farmsteads adorned with vibrant flower boxes and heritage wayside shrines, an awe-inspiring vista unfolds to the west: the pale limestone battlements of the Wilder Kaiser massif tower majestically over the Leukental basin. Bathed in abundant sunshine, the Römerweg represents a premier year-round promenade for walkers of all fitness levels.

Route & Requirements

The Römerweg delivers a relaxed, highly versatile excursion ideal for families, casual strollers, and active seniors. The full traverse departs Kitzbühel town center (rail station or Liebfrauenkirche), winding through historic hamlet lanes via Lebenberg and open meadow contours to Oberndorf before concluding in the bustling market square of St. Johann in Tirol (total distance approx. 12 km, walking time 3 to 3.5 hours, 180 vertical meters total climb, easy grade T1). The terrain transitions smoothly between quiet paved farm lanes, well-graded gravel walking trails, and pleasant woodland paths (sections are well suited for all-terrain strollers). A distinctive advantage is logistical flexibility: because the regional railway line parallels the route along the valley floor, hikers can begin, truncate, or reverse their walk at any railway station (such as Oberndorf in Tirol). Comfortable sneakers or light walking shoes with reliable tread suffice. Leashed dogs are permitted along the entire trail.

Visit & Arrival

Public transit connectivity via ÖBB and regional trains is flawless: Kitzbühel, Oberndorf in Tirol, and St. Johann in Tirol are served by frequent half-hourly trains along the Innsbruck–Salzburg rail axis. Walkers can leave vehicles at one station and return effortlessly by rail in under ten minutes following their hike. Motorists arrive via the Inntal autobahn A12 (exit Wörgl-Ost), connecting along highways B170 and B161. Pay parking is available at the stations in both towns. The Römerweg is accessible year-round free of charge and remains partially cleared during winter months.

Tips

Stop halfway along the route at the historic Gasthof Römerhof or Pointenhof farm tavern to relish an authentic Tyrolean cold cuts platter ("Marend") featuring alpine cheeses and farmhouse rye bread on the panoramic terrace facing the Wilder Kaiser. In late spring, flowering apple and cherry orchards along the route create a fairytale alpine landscape.
saison: Ganzjährig begehbar (im Winter teilweise als Winterwanderweg geräumt)
